title: Psalm 143 (Septuagint) = Psalm 144 (KJV)
description: Psalm 143 in the Septuagint numbering (Psalm 144 in the KJV). Both the manuscript page scan AND the Greek text are taken directly from Codex Sinaiticus (4th century AD) via the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). The Greek transcription preserves the actual uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra abbreviations, and lectional marks of the manuscript. Library folio: 126. English translation verbatim from the King James Version (1611, public domain) via bible-api.com.
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library, with the manuscript text drawn directly from the same source as the scan:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio of Codex Sinaiticus containing this passage, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Library folio reference: 126.
  2. Original text: The verbatim transcription of the Sinaiticus manuscript from the Codex Sinaiticus Project, preserving uncial forms, lunate sigma, nomina sacra (e.g. ⟨θϲ⟩ = θεός), and scribal marks. Nomina sacra are shown in angle brackets to indicate the manuscript's sacred-name abbreviations.
  3. English translation: The King James Version (1611), retrieved verbatim from the public-domain bible-api.com endpoint.

Numbering: Codex Sinaiticus follows the Septuagint Psalter, in which this is Psalm 143. In the Hebrew and King James numbering the same psalm is Psalm 144. Verse numbers align between the Greek and the KJV in this psalm. The Greek and English in each section are the same words of the same psalm.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>τω δαδ ευλογητοϲ κϲ ο θϲ μου ο διδαϲκων ταϲ χιραϲ μου ειϲ παραταξιν τουϲ δακτυλουϲ μου ειϲ πολεμον <sup>2</sup>ελεοϲ μου και καταφυγη μου αντιλημπτωρ μου και ρυϲτηϲ μου ϋπεραϲπιϲτηϲ μου και επ αυτω ηλπιϲα ϋποταϲϲων τον λαον ϲου ϋπ εμε <sup>3</sup>κε τι εϲτιν ανθρωποϲ οτι εγνωριϲθηϲ αυτω η ϋϊοϲ ανθρωπου οτι λογιζη αυτον <sup>4</sup>ανθρωποϲ ματαιοτητι ωμοιωθη αι ημεραι αυτου ωϲι ϲκια παραγουϲι <sup>5</sup>κε κλινον ουρανουϲ ϲου και καταβηθι αψαι των ορεων και καπνιϲθηϲονται
translation.text:
<sup>1</sup>Blessed
be the LORD my strength, which teacheth my hands to war,
and my fingers to fight: <sup>2</sup>My goodness, and my fortress; my high tower, and my deliverer; my shield, and
he in whom I trust; who subdueth my people under me. <sup>3</sup>LORD, what
is man, that thou takest knowledge of him!
or the son of man, that thou makest account of him! <sup>4</sup>Man is like to vanity: his days
are as a shadow that passeth away. <sup>5</sup>Bow thy heavens, O LORD, and come down: touch the mountains, and they shall smoke.

translation.original_text: <sup>6</sup>αϲτραψον αϲτραπην και ϲκορπιειϲ αυτουϲ εξαποϲτιλον τα βελη ϲου και ϲυνταραξειϲ αυτουϲ <sup>7</sup>εξαποϲτιλον την χειρα ϲου εξ υψουϲ εξελου με και ρυϲε με εξ υδατων πολλων εκ χειροϲ ϋϊων αλλοτριων <sup>8</sup>ων το ϲτομα ελαληϲεν ματαιοτητα και η δεξια αυτων δεξια αδικιαϲ <sup>9</sup>ο θϲ ωδην καινην αϲομαι ϲοι εν ψαλτηριω δεκαχορδω ψαλω ϲοι <sup>10</sup>τω διδοντι την ϲωτηριαν τοιϲ βαϲιλευϲιν τω λυτρουμενω δαδ τον δουλον αυτου εκ ρομφαιαϲ πονηραϲ
translation.text:
<sup>6</sup>Cast forth lightning, and scatter them: shoot out thine arrows, and destroy them. <sup>7</sup>Send thine hand from above; rid me, and deliver me out of great waters, from the hand of strange children; <sup>8</sup>Whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand
is a right hand of falsehood. <sup>9</sup>I will sing a new song unto thee, O God: upon a psaltery
and
 an instrument of ten strings will I sing praises unto thee. <sup>10</sup>It is he that giveth salvation unto kings: who delivereth David his servant from the hurtful sword.

translation.original_text: <sup>11</sup>ρυϲαι με και εκ χειροϲ ϋϊων αλλοτριων ων το ϲτομα ελαληϲεν ματαιοτητα και η δεξια αυτων δεξια αδικιαϲ <sup>12</sup>ων ϋϊοι ωϲ νεοφυτα ηδρυμμενα εν τη νεοτητι αυτων αι θυγατερεϲ αυτων κεκαλλωπιϲμεναι περικεκοϲμημεναι ωϲ ομοιωμα ναου <sup>13</sup>τα ταμεια αυτων πληρη εξερευγομενα εκ τουτου του ειϲ τουτο τα προβατα αυτων πλυτοκα πληθυνοντα εν ταιϲ εξοδοιϲ αυτων <sup>14</sup>οι βοεϲ αυτων παχειϲ ουκ εϲτιν καταπτωμα φραγμου ουδε διεξοδοϲ ουδε κραυγη εν ταιϲ επαυλεϲιν αυτω <sup>15</sup>εμακαριϲα τον λαον ω ταυτα εϲτιν μακαριοϲ ο λαοϲ ϲου κϲ ο θϲ αυτου εϲτι
translation.text:
<sup>11</sup>Rid me, and deliver me from the hand of strange children, whose mouth speaketh vanity, and their right hand
is a right hand of falsehood: <sup>12</sup>That our sons
may be as plants grown up in their youth;
that our daughters
may be as corner stones, polished
after the similitude of a palace: <sup>13</sup>That our garners
may be full, affording all manner of store:
that our sheep may bring forth thousands and ten thousands in our streets: <sup>14</sup>That our oxen
may be strong to labour;
that there be no breaking in, nor going out; that
there be no complaining in our streets. <sup>15</sup>Happy
is that people, that is in such a case:
yea,
 happy
is that people, whose God
is the LORD.

verification.section_folios_note: Each section links to the specific folio(s) containing its verses, resolved per verse via the Codex Sinaiticus Project page index.
